channel.title: Rory Millard — writing
channel.description: Essays and working notes on Bayesian search, sensing and decisions under uncertainty, including the ABYSSAL series.

item.title: MH370 in ABYSSAL: Live Evidence Fusion, 3D Surface, Raw Physics & Residual Search
item.description: Running Malaysia Airlines flight 370 inside ABYSSAL's Ember workspace on real public data: full-detail 7th arc map, 3D probability surface, live evidence toggling, provenance fusion graphs, movement & time drift, Ops wind/currents/relief, Satellite View, Plan Studio, Where next, pixel-measured ATSB sonar coverage, 36 years of NOAA drifters, IMOS hydrophones, FDSN seismometers, MODIS/Jason-2/WSPR null tests.

item.title: ABYSSAL on real data: seven studies, with receipts
item.description: ABYSSAL's engines run on real satellite radar, survey bathymetry, Sentinel-2 imagery and public records, scored against truth they never saw: buoys, ship transponders, nautical charts and a real wreck.

item.title: Inside ABYSSAL: one contract, sixteen engines
item.description: The whole of ABYSSAL in one chart: inputs with receipts, sixteen physics-based signal engines that share one contract, an admission gate, a log-space belief engine and the decisions on top. Plus every engine, with screenshots, maths and calibration.

item.title: The Fifth Miss
item.description: A small experiment in negative evidence: how shared sensor failures change what repeated misses tell you, with an interactive model.

item.title: Building it honestly
item.description: The rules that keep ABYSSAL honest: invariants, the engine audit, the calibration gate, the mistakes they were written to prevent, and where calibrated probability over space and time is worth paying for.

item.title: Three cases, two refusals
item.description: ABYSSAL's three reference cases: the Merchant Royal (1641) and the uncertainty of a seventeenth-century league, MH370's satellite arcs and a particle filter that refused to publish, and a chronological held-out backtest of the AF447 search with its hindsight-bias traps.

item.title: The operating picture
item.description: A tour of ABYSSAL's Ops console: live ADS-B and AIS, dark-vessel and orbiting-aircraft flags, SGP4 satellites, environmental layers, leeway drift, bearings fixes, shadow chronolocation, track-gap reach ellipses, and the multi-target watchlist.

item.title: Signals from the deep
item.description: The physics behind ABYSSAL's Signal Lab: SAR ship detection, Kelvin wakes and the azimuth shift, AIS association and dark vessels, hydroacoustic TDOA localisation, ring detection, calibration, and impact ring waves as a dispersive clock.

item.title: Where next, and when to stop
item.description: Optimal search allocation (water-filling), expected value of information, mutual information per pound, the search-to-exhaustion curve and stopping rules in ABYSSAL's Where-next and Plan Studio.

item.title: Five echoes, one witness
item.description: An essay on correlated evidence and provenance in ABYSSAL: geometric pooling of same-source reports, per-item versus whole-source influence in bits, and why humans must admit evidence.

item.title: The arithmetic of not finding
item.description: The mathematics of Bayesian search in ABYSSAL: log-space grid updates, negative evidence, the coverage fallacy, contamination likelihoods, repeat credit, KL divergence in bits and minimum-KL area statements.

item.title: A map that refuses to lie
item.description: The design of ABYSSAL's map: the context/evidence firewall, perceptually ordered colour, credible regions, honest resolution, sketching evidence on the map, certain area statements and offline audit packs.

item.title: Finding what is lost: a tour of ABYSSAL
item.description: A guided, screenshot-led tour of ABYSSAL, a local-first Bayesian search workbench for finding lost aircraft, ships and people.
